description:
The q67.21.9-.13 arc changed what several components ARE. Their names still describe what they were. This ticket lands the renames LAST, once the purposes have settled, so nothing is renamed twice.

Names in this project are truth, not labels — the same standard applied to comments. Each rename below is justified by a purpose that CHANGED; churn for its own sake is explicitly out of scope (see NOT RENAMING).

1. materializer_refs -> materializer_members (21 references in lib/)
bedrock-q67.21.9 made membership set-valued: the value is %{worker_id => node}, a member SET, and the decoder is already Reader.decode_materializer_members/1. The carrier fields never followed:
- Distributor.State snapshot field materializer_refs (state.ex:21) and every reader (server.ex:341,384,400,402,408, transactions.ex:119,135)
- 'refs' was accurate when the family was single-valued and the value was a {worker_id, node} REF. It is now a set, and 'ref' actively misleads: it reads as one callable thing.

2. RecoveryAttempt.shard_materializers -> system_shard_members, and prior_materializer_refs deleted
After bedrock-q67.21.13 recovery establishes ONLY tag 0, so 'shard_materializers' (plural shards) names something that no longer exists. prior_materializer_refs disappears entirely with the persistence diff. Also rename bootstrap's to_materializer_refs/1 accordingly — it emits member maps as of q67.21.9 and its name predates that.

3. MaterializerBootstrapPhase -> SystemShardBootstrapPhase
After bedrock-q67.21.13 the phase bootstraps the system shard and nothing else: it exists so recovery can READ the metadata families, not to place materializers. The current name promises data-plane placement that now belongs to the distributor.

4. TSLValidationPhase -> CoreStateValidationPhase; TSLTypeValidator -> CoreStateValidator
It already validates the durable record, not the broadcast: it runs on old_transaction_system_layout (tsl_validation_phase.ex:46) and validate_type_safety/1 (tsl_type_validator.ex:22-26) calls exactly validate_logs and validate_resolvers — the value has no :resolvers, so it validates precisely the log record. After bedrock-q67.21.11 that value IS CoreState, and the name should say so.
FIX THE MODULEDOC IN THE SAME PASS: it claims to validate version_vector and durable_version. The code checks neither, and never has. Pre-existing drift; this is the right moment.

5. SystemKeys.ClusterBootstrap — decide, do not drift
It is the on-disk FlatBuffer schema backing CoreState after bedrock-q67.21.11/.12. Either keep ClusterBootstrap as the WIRE format name (defensible: it is also what a cold-starting node reads to discover its role) and document that CoreState is its in-memory projection, or rename to match. Pick one deliberately and write the reason down; the failure mode here is two names drifting apart with no stated relationship.

NOT RENAMING (recorded so it is not relitigated):
- TransactionSystemLayout — accurate for what it becomes: the per-recovery broadcast wiring, FDB's ServerDBInfo. Established across the codebase; renaming buys nothing.
- Distributor — FDB's DataDistributor analogue, already accurate.
- Placeholder — accurate; it is an ordinary member of the set that parks reads.
- RoutingData.materializers — a map of tag => members, and the accessor materializer_members/2 already says so.

SEQUENCING: lands after bedrock-q67.21.13. Renaming before the semantics settle means renaming twice and conflicting with the in-flight stack. Pure rename PR: no behavior change, so a green suite with no test-expectation edits (beyond names) is the correctness argument.
title: Rename components to match their clarified purposes
